texts: At midnight the Keeper checks the flame.
At midnight the Keeper refills the reservoir to the half-mark.
At the third watch the Keeper trims the wick carefully.
A wick carbonizes over a long burn.
At dawn the Keeper extinguishes the flame with a brass snuffer.
The Keeper walks home after dawn-out.

fields.sentence: At midnight the Keeper checks the flame.

review.notes: 'the Keeper' takes the capitalized-common-noun default, the bare simple present correctly gets no status atom (habitual/unmarked), and 'check' is an evaluate/record verb so Theme is right. 'midnight' is not in the instruction set's day-part constant list (dawn/noon/dusk/night) though it follows that pattern, leaving the choice between a bare Time constant and an (Hour 0) clock term undetermined.

fields.sentence: At midnight the Keeper refills the reservoir to the half-mark.

review.notes: 'the Keeper' correctly takes the capitalized-common-noun default (no Name atom), 'at midnight' stays a bare Time symbol with no tense atom (habitual/unmarked), and half_mark emits its head genus while correctly withholding the non-predicable modifier 'half'. 'to the half-mark' is a fill-LEVEL endpoint that MeasureTo cannot carry (its slots need magnitude + unit), so Goal — licensed for a non-recipient 'to …' — is the only available head; borderline against the 'an end value is never a spatial Goal' clause, but defensible.

fields.sentence: At the third watch the Keeper trims the wick carefully.

review.notes: "At the third watch" as the bare Time constant third_watch follows the named-time / period precedent (first_quarter), and no Every atom is added since no "every" is present. Manner keeps the surface -ly form "carefully", and no PartOf between the wick and any lantern is invented.

fields.sentence: A wick carbonizes over a long burn.

review.notes: 'A wick' with a verbal predicate is correctly a witness rather than a generic rule, and the bare simple present correctly carries no status atom (the unmarked dispositional default). 'over' is not one of the three words that license During, so the surface-preposition oblique (Over e ...) is the right head.

fields.sentence: At dawn the Keeper extinguishes the flame with a brass snuffer.

review.notes: brass_snuffer fuses with only the head genus, correct because "brass" is a noun modifier and noun modifiers are never exposed; "the Keeper" takes the capitalized-common-noun default with no Name atom. The bare present with an unanchored "at dawn" correctly gets no tense atom and no Every, and dawn rides Time as a day-part constant.

fields.sentence: The Keeper walks home after dawn-out.

review.notes: 'The Keeper' correctly takes the capitalized-common-noun default (witness + kind atom, no Name), the bare simple present correctly gets no status atom, and 'after dawn-out' becomes Before with the arguments swapped. The temporal-anchor event noun carries only its class atom and the ordering relation, and dawn_out correctly gets no genus since 'out' is not a head noun.
